chunks: Abu Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Askari narrated to us, saying: Abu'l-Qasem Badr ibn al-Haytham the judge narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Mundhir al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl narrated from Abu al-Sabah, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said:

The one who is given four will not be deprived of four: The one who is given supplication will not be deprived of response; and the one who is given seeking forgiveness will not be deprived of repentance; and the one who is given gratitude will not be deprived of increase; and the one who is given patience will not be deprived of reward.
ai.seo_question: What are the four spiritual gifts that guarantee their corresponding divine rewards according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates a profound spiritual reciprocity where the divine bestowal of the capacity for worship guarantees its acceptance, framing these acts as divine gifts rather than mere human efforts. This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, emphasizes that gratitude (Shukr) and patience (Sabr) are not only virtues but mechanisms for divine increase and reward, reinforcing the Shia understanding of God's generosity in response to human devotion. The chain of narration highlights the scholarly transmission of this principle within the Ahl al-Bayt tradition, linking the believer's internal state directly to external divine favor.
